title: Cedar and rose wardrobe sachets
subtitle: Cedar chips and dried rosebuds for clothes storage
excerpt: Cedar and rose wardrobe sachets are small bags filled with cedar wood chips, dried rosebuds, and a few drops of cedarwood essential oil to reinforce the scent. Cedar naturally deters moths; the rose adds a light floral note that makes the sachets pleasant to have among clothes. Each sachet contains about 20 g of filling; replenish the essential oil every three to four months when the cedar fades.
sourceNotes: Cedar as a moth deterrent: the cedrol in cedarwood (Cedrus atlantica) has been documented as a natural moth deterrent since at least Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861). Cedar shavings in sachets: The Pot-Pourri Book by Penny Black (1989, Simon & Schuster). Dried rosebuds as a fragrance addition: traditional British linen cupboard practice. Cedar essential oil for refreshing sachets when the wood fades: The Complete Book of Essential Oils and Aromatherapy by Valerie Wormwood (1991).

recipe.batchNotes: Fill as many sachets as needed from a larger batch.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use immediately once filled and tied. The fresh cedar scent is strongest in the first few weeks.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: The sachets last two years or more if refreshed every three to four months. Replenish by opening the sachet and adding five to eight drops of cedarwood essential oil, then closing and leaving for a day before replacing in the wardrobe. Replace the filling after two years.

glossaryTerms.definition: Small chips or shavings of cedarwood used in sachets and drawers as a natural moth deterrent and fragrance source. The cedar scent fades over time and can be refreshed with a few drops of cedarwood essential oil.

items.prepNote: untreated cedar chips or shavings from a craft or pet supply, not chemically treated cedar for animal bedding
dried whole rosebuds; mix through the cedar before filling
~5 drops per sachet; drip onto the cedar chips and allow to absorb for 30 minutes before filling the sachets

content.text: Spread the cedar chips in a shallow bowl or tray. Drip the cedarwood essential oil over the chips, about five drops per 15 g of chips, and toss to distribute. Leave for 30 minutes for the oil to absorb before handling. Mix the dried rosebuds through the cedar. Fill four small muslin drawstring bags or fabric squares (about 10 × 10 cm) with 20 g of the blend each. Tie or sew closed.

Hang one sachet from a rail in the wardrobe, or place in a corner of a shelf or drawer. The cedar should be close to (but not touching) natural fibre clothing, wool and cashmere are the fabrics moths target. Replace sachets in summer, before moths are active.

When the cedar scent fades, typically after three to four months, open the sachet and add five to eight drops of cedarwood essential oil directly onto the chips. Close the sachet and leave it out of the wardrobe for one day to allow the oil to absorb before replacing. This extends the sachet's life by another three to four months.
Two years or more if refreshed regularly. Replace the filling when the cedar chips become very pale and the scent does not return even with new essential oil drops.
